author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Haba nga ïaid lyngba ka ri khlaw jong kane ka pyrthei, nga la poi ha kawei ka jaka kaba don ka krem.
english: As I walked through the wilderness of this world, I lighted on a certain place where was a den.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Nga la thiah ha kata ka jaka ban shongthait, bad haba nga la ïohthiah nga la phohsniew.
english: I laid me down in that place to sleep; and, as I slept, I dreamed a dream.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Ha kata ka jingphohsniew nga la ïohi ïa uwei u briew uba da kup da ki jaiñ jot.
english: I dreamed, and behold, I saw a man clothed with rags.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: U ïeng bad ka khmat jong u ka phai sha lyndet na la ka jong ka ïing.
english: Standing in a certain place, with his face turned away from his own house.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: U bat kawei ka kot ha la ka kti, bad kawei ka jingkit kaba khia halor ka met jong u.
english: A book in his hand, and a great heavy burden upon his back.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Nga la khmih bad nga la ïohi ba u la plied ïa kata ka kot bad u la pule ha ka.
english: I looked, and saw him open the book and read therein.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Katba u dang pule u la ïam bad u la khynñiuh da ka jingsheptieng.
english: And, as he read, he wept, and trembled with exceeding fear.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: U khlem lah shuh ban theh lade, bad u la pyrta da ka sur kaba sngewsih, Kaei ngan leh?
english: Unable longer to contain himself, he broke out with a lamentable cry, saying, What shall I do?

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: U la leit phai sha la ka ïing, hynrei um lah shuh ban buhrieh ïa la ka jingsngewsih na la ka tnga bad ki khun.
english: In this plight, therefore, he went home to his house, but could not long conceal his sorrow from his wife and children.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: U la ong ha ki, Ko tnga baieit bad ko khun baieit, ka jingkit kaba khia ka la ban ha nga.
english: He said unto them, O my dear wife, and you the children of my bowels, a dreadful burden presseth sore upon me.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: La pyntip ha nga ba kane ka shnong jong ngi kan sa shah bam ha ka ding na bneng.
english: Moreover, I am certainly informed that this our city will be burned with fire from heaven.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Haba ki la ïohsngew ïa kine ki ktien, ki la pyrkhat ba ka khlieh jong u ka la shit noh.
english: At this his relations were sore amazed, thinking some frenzy distemper had got into his head.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Mar ïa ong kumta, nga la ïohi ïa uwei u briew uba kyrteng U Nongiathuhkhana uba la wan ha u.
english: Now, as he was walking in the fields, behold, a man named Evangelist came to him.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: U la kylli ïa u, Balei me ïam bad me pyrta kumne?
english: And asked him, Wherefore dost thou weep and cry?

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: U la jubab, Ko Saheb, nga pule ha kane ka kot ba nga dei ban ïap bad ban shah bishar ha khmat U Blei.
english: He answered, Sir, I perceive by the book in my hand that I am condemned to die, and after that to come to judgment.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: U Nongiathuhkhana u la ai ha u ïa kawei ka kot kaba thoh, Phet na ka jingbitar kaban sa wan!
english: Then Evangelist gave him a parchment roll, and there was written within, Flee from the wrath to come!

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: U briew u la kylli, Shano ngan phet?
english: The man therefore read it, and looking upon Evangelist very carefully, said, Whither must I fly?

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: U Nongiathuhkhana u la kdew da ka shynriahti, Me ïohi ïatai ka khyrdop ba rit sha jngai?
english: Then said Evangelist, pointing with his finger over a very wide field, Do you see yonder Wicket-gate?

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: U briew u la ong, Em, ngam ïohi bha, hynrei nga ïohi ïa ka jingshai kaba phyrnai.
english: The man said, No, I do not see it; but methinks I see a shining light.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Ong U Nongiathuhkhana, Khmih sah ïatai ka jingshai bad mareh beit beit sha ka.
english: Keep that light in your eye, and go up directly thereto: so shalt thou see the gate.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Katba ki dang ïaid lyngba ka madan, ki la poi harud kawei ka ktieh kaba jur kaba kyrteng Ka Bir Jingduh-Jingkyrmen.
english: Now, as they drew near, they drew towards a miry slough that was in the midst of the plain, the name of which was Despond.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Ki la ngam shapoh jong ka khlem da kheiñ, namar kim shym la phikir ïa la ki kjat.
english: And being heedless, they did both fall suddenly into the bog.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: U Pilgrim u la ngam kham jylliew namar kata ka jingkit kaba khia kaba don halor ka met jong u.
english: Here Christian began to sink in the mire, because of the great burden that was on his back.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Hynrei uwei u briew uba kyrteng U Nongïarap u la wan bad u la shim ïa ka kti jong u ban ring ïa u na kata ka ktieh.
english: Then I saw in my dream, that a man came to him, whose name was Help, and took him by the hand and drew him out.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: U la pynïeng biang ïa u halor ka lynti kaba skhem.
english: And set him upon sound ground, and bid him go on his way.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: U Pilgrim u la kiew shaphrang haduh ba u la poi ha uwei u lum uba don ka Diengphna halor jong u.
english: He ran thus till he came at a place somewhat ascending; and upon that place stood a Cross.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Mar ïa poi u ha khmat kata ka Diengphna, kata ka jingkit ka la dkut bad ka la tyllun noh na ka met jong u.
english: So I saw in my dream, that just as Christian came up with the Cross, his burden loosed from off his shoulders.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Ka la tyllun shapoh kawei ka jingtep kaba jylliew, bad um shym la ïohi shuh ïa ka.
english: And fell from off his back, and began to tumble, and so continued to do till it came to the mouth of the sepulchre, where it fell in, and I saw it no more.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Te u Pilgrim u la kmen shibun eh bad u la shad da ka jingkmen ha la ka dohnud.
english: Then was Christian glad and lightsome, and said with a merry heart, He hath given me rest by his sorrow.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: U la rwai da ka sur kaba bang, U la pynlait ïa nga na ka jingkit ka jong nga!
english: Then he gave three leaps for joy, and went out singing, Blest Cross! blest Sepulchre! blest rather be the Man that there was put to shame for me!

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Ha kata ka miet u la poi ha kawei ka ïingkham kaba bhabriew kaba don harud ka lynti.
english: So I saw in my dream that he made haste and went forward, and came to the Palace Beautiful by the highway side.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Ki samla kynthei kiba kyrteng Ka Jingstad, Ka Jingakorbha, bad Ka Jingieit ki la pdiang sngewbha ïa u.
english: The fair maidens Piety, Prudence, and Charity opened the doors and welcomed him in.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Ki la ai ha u ïa ki jaiñ-riam thma kiba kynthup ïa ka stieh jong ka jingngeit bad ka waitlam jong ka ktien.
english: They led him into the armoury, and showed him all manner of weapons: the shield of faith and the sword of the spirit.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Haba u la hiar sha ka Them Sngewrit, u la ïashem bad uwei u ksuid uba shyrkhei uba kyrteng U Apollyon.
english: In the Valley of Humiliation, poor Christian was hard put to it; for he had gone but a little way before he espied a foul fiend coming to meet him, named Apollyon.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: U Apollyon u la pyrshang ban pynduh-mynsiem ïa u bad ban phai dien ïa u sha ka Shnong Jingjot.
english: Apollyon sought to break his spirit and force him to return back to the City of Destruction.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Hynrei u Pilgrim u la bat skhem ïa la ka waitlam bad u la pyndonkam ïa ka stieh ban ïada ïa lade.
english: Christian nimbly drew his sword and caught the shield, making noble defence against the darts of the dragon.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Hadien ka jingïaleh kaba jur, u Apollyon u la phet noh bad u la iehnoh ïa u ha ka jingsuk.
english: With that Apollyon spread forth his dragon wings, and sped him away, that Christian for a season saw him no more.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Hadien kane ki la poi ha kawei ka shnong kaba don ka ïew kaba heh kaba kyrteng Ka Ïew Kai-kam.
english: Almost as soon as they were got out of the wilderness, they saw a town before them, named Vanity; and at that town there is a fair kept, called Vanity Fair.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Ha kata ka ïew la die ïa ki jingthala baroh: ka spah, ka nam, ka burom, bad ki jinglehbyrngia jong kane ka pyrthei.
english: At this fair are all such merchandise sold as houses, lands, trades, places, honours, preferments, titles, and all kinds of worldly delights.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Ki nongïew ki la pynsalia ïa u Pilgrim bad u Faithful namar ba ki jaiñkup jong ki ki ïapher bad kim kwah thied ïa ki tiar jong ka ïew.
english: The fair-goers made a great hubbub about them, because their apparel was so different and they set light by all their worldly wares.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: U Faithful u la ïeng skhem ha la ka jingngeit bad u la shah pynïap noh da ka jingthang ha ka ding ha khmat ki briew.
english: Faithful stood fast in his confession of truth and was condemned to be burned to ashes at the stake before the angry mob.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Hynrei kawei ka kali ksiar ka la wan ban shim ïa u Faithful beit sha ka Shnong Bneng.
english: Now I saw that there stood behind the multitude a chariot and a couple of horses waiting for Faithful, which carried him up straight through the clouds to the celestial gate.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Katba ki dang ïaid lyngba ka madan By-path, ki la thiah ha u phlang bad la kem ïa ki da u Riewkhraw Jingduh-Jingkyrmen.
english: Now, a little before them there was a stile, and they fell asleep; and Giant Despair, walking in his fields, caught them trespassing upon his grounds.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: U la ring ïa ki sha la ka Kut kaba dum bad u la thep ïa ki ha ka patok kaba jylliew bad ba sma.
english: He therefore drove them before him, and put them into his castle, into a very dark dungeon, nasty and stinking to the spirits of these two men.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: U Pilgrim u la kynmaw ba u don kawei ka shabi ha la ka pla kaba kyrteng Ka Kular.
english: Now, a little before day, good Christian, as one half amazed, brake out in this passionate speech: I have a key in my bosom, called Promise, that will open any lock in Doubting Castle.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Da kata ka shabi ki la plied ïa ki jingkhang baroh jong kata ka kut bad ki la phet lait ha ka jingsuk.
english: Then Christian pulled it out of his bosom, and turned the lock, and the door flew open with ease, and they escaped swiftly into the King's highway.

author: John Bunyan / Rev. Thomas Jones / Dr. John Roberts / Mondon Bareh
khasi: Ki la kiew halor ki Lum Bhabriew bad ki la khmih sha jngai ïa ka kynroh jong ka Shnong Bneng.
english: Then they went up into the Delectable Mountains to behold the gardens and orchards, and looked through the perspective glass toward the Celestial City.
